newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firm after expiry as crude leads.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firm after expiry as crude leads.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed sharply firmer on Monday, pulled higher by a strong performance on crude markets in both London and New York, dealers said.
June gas oil closed $6.25 firmer at $173.50 a tonne, trimming the June/July contango by 50 cents.
Gas oil sentiment was also lifted by a smaller than expected delivery into the May contract, which expired at midday.
A total of 97,100 tonnes of gas oil would be delivered into the contract, an IPE source said, significantly undercutting dealers pre-expiry estimates of between 200,000 and 500,000 tonnes.

But dealers said most of gas oil's strength came from the rally in Brent crude, which hit two-month highs in afternoon dealing on investment fund buying in New York, tension in the Middle East and talk of thin North Sea June supply.
June Brent crude was 64 cents firmer at $19.57 a barrel by 1718 GMT, just eight cents off the high for the day and at levels not seen since the middle of March.

Last week's rally prompted fresh buying by fund managers, extending early gains posted on the back of Iranian war games in the Gulf and talk of maintenance cutting into North Sea output next month, dealers said.
